_: Settlement sheet for Riverwalk (2.5c), from its place record.

norms.text: The way across the cove is sounded with a pole every morning, before the first boat.
Boat crews are fed and given a bunk; the village grows no food of its own.
Boards on the plank walk are replaced one at a time, when they go soft.

taboos.text: Paying the toll to Thorn's or Hissmir's agent directly; it counts as taking a side.
Mooring across the stage when a canoe is due out.

values.text: A full table for whoever lands, crew or passenger.
Sheltered water, which nothing else on this coast offers.

contempts.text: Crews who leave without settling for their bunk.
Agents from Thorn who walk out to the spit to argue the toll.

place.text: A small cove with the only safe water on the coast; the boats have to come here.

work.text: Feeding crews and taking fares is steady work while the boats keep coming.

trade.text: Every boat off the Padomaic run leaves coin at the stage.

danger.text: The cove itself is safe water; silt is the worry. We sound the way every morning.

directions.text: Thorn is up the Tear road; Hissmir is up the pilgrim water by canoe.

faction.text: Thorn and Hissmir both want the toll. The village sits caught between them.

addressTerms.text: Crews are called by their boat; passengers are 'traveller' until fed.

grievances.text: Thorn's field-owners and Hissmir's stewards each say the toll is theirs.

rumours.text: The toll argument at the spit grows louder each night.

views.text: Pilgrims bound for Hissmir pass through and eat well first.

dissent.text: Poles the raft through the toll every crossing; the toll comes out of the crew's share.
Writes each boat in two columns and knows the levy funds a quarrel as much as the state.
